title: More models, more control over chat
summary:
The week made Pollinations easier to build with: more capable chat requests, sturdier image generation, a community chat app, and clearer Pollen controls.

Claude Sonnet 4.5 joined as `claude-large` and Grok 4 Fast as `grok`, both with tool support. Chat gained `reasoning_effort` and `thinking_budget`, including pass-through of provider reasoning fields in streamed responses. Perplexity citation URLs and other provider-specific fields now survive the proxy, while clearer upstream errors make failed requests less of a guessing game. A shared `openai` default now governs chat completions when no model is specified.

Exact-match image caching moved into Enter: a hit returns the stored image without another key or rate-limit check, while a miss follows the usual generation path. Related fixes cover empty cache entries and responses without a Content-Length header. Image requests also gained retries for ComfyUI HTTP 500s, server-side fetching of Seedream reference images, and better handling of slashes and UTF-8 in prompts. The image service added persistent request counts by model at `/model-stats`.

The $5, $10, $20, and $50 Pollen pack buttons were connected to checkout. Enter’s tier panel now distinguishes active subscriptions from target tiers, shows cancellation end dates, and reports activation and lookup errors more clearly. Spore was added ahead of Seed as the default tier for new accounts, alongside updated Pollen guidance.

CloudCompile’s chat interface joined the repo with selectable models, saved conversations, themes, speech input, and markdown rendering. Follow-up work added pasted and dropped images, model search, streaming replies, and mobile improvements. The drawing-to-code panel remains a placeholder; not every button needs to pretend it has a backend.
